In this work, the hybrid kinase MA4377 from the methanogenic archaeon 28

Methanosarcina acetivorans was investigated (2, 3). MA4377 is a multidomain 29 protein resembling a bacterial-type histidine kinase with two additional receiver 30 domains at the C-terminus. Recombinant protein was employed to investigate the 31 intra-and intermolecular phosphorelay in vitro. The kinase displays 32 autophosphorylation activity of histidine residue 497. While no intramolecular 33 phosphorelay was observed, the CheY-like receiver protein MA4376 was identified 34 as part of the multi-component system that also seems to include the Msr-type 35 transcription factor MA4375. Introduction 40

In order for organisms to survive, it is essential to rapidly react to environmental 41 changes by perceiving and processing signals, thereby triggering an adequate 42 cellular response. In bacteria, the most commonly used signal transduction system 43 is the phosphorelay of two-components consisting of a sensory histidine kinase 44 (HK) and a response regulator (RR) (4-8). After perceiving a signal, the kinase 45 gets autophosphorylated at a conserved histidine residue (His1). Subsequently, 46 the phosphoryl group is transferred to a conserved aspartate residue (Asp1) in the 47 receiver domain (REC) of the cognate RR ( Fig. 1) (4, 5, 7, 9). The phosphorylated 48 RR then initiates the cellular response to the perceived signal, most commonly 49 through transcriptional activation/repression. However, RR with an enzymatic 50 function instead of DNA-binding capacity also exist and function as stand-alone 51 receiver (REC) domains (10). transcription factor as the final phosphocomponent in the phosphorelay 308 of MA4377? 309 Single receiver domains of bacteria often rely on protein-protein interaction in order 310 to fulfill their function (25). If fused to DNA binding domains, they are able to 311 regulate transcription (26). Thus far, not much is known about the function of 312 bacterial-type single receiver domains in Archaea. Yet, interaction with another 313 protein partner is conceivable. Therefore, we had another closer look at the 314 genomic localization of the MCS. Downstream of MA4377 and MA4376, the 315 transcription factor (TF) MA4375 is encoded (Fig. 2). MA4375 belongs to the Msr 316 family of archaeal transcription factors and related ones have been identified to be 317 involved in the transcriptional activation of corrinoid-methyltransferase fusion 318 proteins (27). MA4375 has the same structure as the above-mentioned TFs, 319 consisting of a helix-turn-helix (HTH) domain and a domain of unknown function 320 1724 (DUF1724) (27). We therefore asked whether there might be a link between 321 our MCS and the TF MA4375, maybe through transphosphorylation. 322

transduction, whether via a two-or multi-component system 392 involving a phosphorelay, is a well investigated and understood mechanism used 393 by microorganisms in order to respond to environmental changes (4, 6-8). 394However, their function in Archaea is still largely unexplored, owing in part to only 395 a limited number of genetically accessible organisms being available (31). In 396 screening the ever increasing number of genomes being released, it becomes 397 obvious that these signal transduction systems are also present in Archaea, having 398 possibly radiated from Bacteria via horizontal gene transfer (32). Here, the major 399 question arises as to how these systems have adapted to work together with the 400 archaeal transcription machinery, which possesses components related to that of 401Bacteria and Eukarya but still being distinct from either. In fact, the archaeal RNA 402 polymerase structurally and evolutionarily resembles eukaryotic RNA polymerase 403 II (33, 34). This study made progress in investigating and understanding of a 404 bacterial-type phosphorelay system in a methanogenic archaeon M. acetivorans 405 (3). Using in vitro phosphorylation experiments with recombinant protein, we were 406 able to show the autokinase activity of the hybrid kinase MA4377. Although the 407 two fused receiver domains at the C-terminus of the MA4377 protein are not 408 directly involved in the phosphorelay, transphosphorylation to the vicinal encoded 409 single receiver protein, MA4376, was observed. The overlap of 29 nt between both 410 open reading frames might suggest that at some point in their evolution, MA4377 411 and MA4376 were a single ORF encoding a single hybrid kinase with three R 412 domains. The hybrid kinase RodK from Myxococcus xanthus represents such a 413 system, carrying three R domains (35). Only the third R domain is served by an 414 intramolecular phosphotransfer, while the other two are proposed to function as 415 phosphate sinks to modulate the rate of kinase activity inside RodK or to alternative 416 RR in response to incoming signals. Although the authors did not find 417 phosphorylation of R1 and R2 of the Myxococcus xanthus kinase, they provide 418 genetic evidence for the distinct function of all three R domains within RodK, with 419 phosphorylation by other kinases being one possible scenario. In the MA4377 and 420 MA4376 system investigated in this study, no phosphorylation of R1 and R2 of the 421 kinase MA4377 was observed. Only transphosphorylation to the single receiver 422 protein MA4376 was detected. Based on the results generated in this study, we 423 propose that MA4376 serves as a central hub to direct the signal into different 424 directions. While it itself is phosphorylated by the kinase, it furthermore supports 425the phosphotransfer from the kinase to the TF MA4375(Fig. 10). In addition, it is 426 also able to direct the phosphorylation signal back to the kinase. As all results 427obtained in this study were from in vitro experiments in the absence of most signal 428 input domains (PAS domain still present in employed PK construct), it is necessary 429 to include the membrane-bound signaling domains in future studies to confirm the 430 function of MA4377 in vivo. The major signal input domain in MA4377 is likely to 431 be the membrane-bound CHASE domain (36) Although it is widespread in 432 prokaryotes, lower eukaryotes and plants, not much is known about its function. It 433 is predicted to bind various low molecular weight ligands. In the case of MA4377, 434 the CHASE domain might be involved in sensing methylated compounds as 435 alternative substrates for methanogenesis. Data from the Metcalf group support 436 such an assumption (37). This group demonstrated that deletion of the kinase 437 MA4377 and the TF MA4375 in M. acetivorans had a significant impact on the 438 transcription of the corrinoid-methyltransferase gene mtsF (MA4384), with 439 transcription being upregulated when cells were grown on the alternative substrate 440 trimethylamine (TMA). The synthesis of MtsF was furthermore influenced by the 441 redox-responsive kinase, MsmS (17), indicating that MA4377-MA4376-MA4375 442 and MsmS might belong to one large signal transduction network. This system 443 furthermore also includes RdmS as a signal input kinase in M. acetivorans (Fig. 444 12), as its deletion had an impact on the transcription of mtsD when cells are grown 445 in methanol (18, 37) Interestingly, the kinases MsmS and RdmS are not bacterial-446 type histidine-kinases and their downstream signal transduction sequence is Schematic overview of the methanogenesis related signal transduction system mentioned 450 in the discussion. The genetic organization of kinases, TF and corrinoid methyltransferases are shown as 451 arrows indicating the direction of transcription. 452 453 More experiments are needed to clarify whether the receiver MA4376 serves as a 454 central hub in connecting the kinases MsmS, RdmS and MA4377 with the 455 respective TF MA4375, MsrC, MsrF and MsrG, thereby regulating methylotrophic 456 methanogenesis. Genomic analysis revealed an abundance of 4000 histidine 81 kinases and regulators in 218 archaeal genomes. None were however identified in 82 the Cren-, Kor-and Nanoarchaeota. This shows a relatively high abundance of TCS in Archaea. Thus far, 87 only a few signaling systems have been investigated within the methanogens. 88 Among them, the TCS LtrK/R of Methanococcoides burtonii, which is involved in 89 temperature-response (14).
